subject: Sizing questionnaire: Streamly preflight for microburst-heavy convo bursts
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena@streamly.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Streamly preflight: sizing questionnaire and sample telemetry request

Hi Lena — great to meet on Friday. As discussed, we want to size a Dedicated deployment that handles Streamly's conversational product workload (lots of short queries + occasional long generations). To make the initial sizing fast and precise, could you send back the short questionnaire below and any sample telemetry you have (token histograms, a small sample of prompts/responses, and a representative 24–72h traffic trace if possible). I attached a short Microburst SLA template for reference.

Key asks (can be rough estimates):
- Typical session pattern: average prompts / session, session duration, idle time distribution
- Prompt length distribution (tokens) and typical response token length
- Peak concurrent sessions and sustained concurrency (1h average vs 5m peaks)
- Burst characteristics: multiplier over baseline, typical burst duration, cadence (e.g., hourly spikes, event-driven)
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p90/p99) and whether p99 is a hard SLA
- Feature notes: use of caching/KV reuse, multi-turn chat with long KV cache keys, model pinning requirements, prefer quantized models?
- Security: will Streamly require Private (VPC) deployment or can you start hosted/dedicated hybrid? Any data residency / SOC2 needs.

If you can return the answers and attach a sample token histogram, we'll sketch a recommended committed fleet + burst pool and propose a short 30-minute sizing workshop. Proposed times: Wed 07/26 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 07/27 14:00–14:30 PT.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena@streamly.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@streamly.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 13:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Streamly preflight: sizing questionnaire and sample telemetry request

Hi Camila — thanks, this is exactly what we need. Answers below and attaching a small token histogram + 500-line prompt sample. We can also export a 48h traffic trace if that helps (will take our infra team ~24h).

Answers (best-effort):
- Session pattern: web/chat sessions average 6 prompts/session; median session duration ~2.5 minutes, many sessions are single-query. Idle gaps between prompts ~8–30s for interactive flows.
- Prompt distribution (tokens): 75% short (1–12 tokens), 20% medium (13–60 tokens), 5% long (200–400 tokens) — long ones are rare multi-document summaries.
- Response tokens: average 60 tokens; 90th percentile ~180 tokens.
- Concurrency: baseline sustained ~450 concurrent active sessions; short-term peaks observed up to ~3,200 concurrent (these are 10–30s microbursts during product notifications and marketing drops).
- Burst characteristics: typical microburst is 8–12x baseline, lasts 5–30s, with clusters over a 10–15 minute window during events. Bursts are mostly read-heavy (short prompts) but inflate concurrency and token ingress simultaneously.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 25–50ms, p90 80–120ms, p99 goal is 200ms (we consider p99 >200ms a degradation).
- Caching/KV: we have some short-term session affinity and could benefit from prefix KV reuse for multi-turn chat (large win if supported).
- Model requirements: prefer open LLaMA-v2 family variants; quantized 4-bit acceptable if latency/cost tradeoffs are favorable.
- Deployment: must be VPC-private for production (SOC2 + HIPAA interest for certain customers). We're open to a hosted pilot but need Private for final.

Attached: streamly_token_histogram.csv, sample_prompts.txt.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Park | Head of Platform | Streamly

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Forwarding Streamly's answers and attachments — request from Lena below. They have sustained ~450 concurrency, bursts to ~3.2k (10–12x), average response ~60 tokens, p99 target 200ms, VPC required for GA.

Can you do an initial sizing sketch for Dedicated with a burst pool? Specific asks:
- Committed capacity (count + SKU) to satisfy sustained 450 concurrency and keep p99 ~200ms for their LLaMA-v2 variant (we can assume quantized MPT-like families but prefer LLaMA-2).
- Burst pool sizing to cover 3.2k peaks (short bursts) while preserving latency — how many extra nodes? Recommend autoscale thresholds / warm pool strategy.
- Any clear wins from KV/prefix caching we should call out (rough % token cost reduction).
- Whether to recommend H100 vs A100-80GB vs 4x A10G mixture for cost/latency tradeoffs.

They want a 30-min sizing workshop — propose Thu 07/27 14:00 PT. I'll coordinate with Lena once we have a quick sketch. Attaching Redwood microburst SLA template for reference.

— Camila

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Streamly preflight: sizing questionnaire and sample telemetry request

Quick initial sizing sketch — rough numbers to drive the workshop:

Assumptions (from Streamly): avg response 60 tokens, avg prompt small, short bursts 8–12x baseline, target p99 ~200ms, model family LLaMA-v2 quantized 4-bit. We'll refine after a short load-run/trace.

Sustained commit sizing (to cover 450 concurrent with headroom for steady-state ~10–20%):
- Recommend committed footprint: 6 x H100 (in Private/VPC). Rationale: H100 provides headroom for larger context KV and higher throughput for quantized LLaMA variants while preserving p99 latency with better kernel throughput.
- If customer chooses lower-cost route (A100-80GB): estimate 8–10 x A100-80GB committed to match throughput at roughly similar latency under steady traffic.

Burst pool (covering microbursts to 3.2k concurrency):
- Recommend a burst pool sized for ~2.5–3x the committed baseline (so +12 H100s) with autoscale to warm additional nodes within 20–40s for the short bursts. Because bursts are so short (5–30s), we recommend a warm standby pool of smaller cheaper SKUs for instant absorb (e.g., 6 x A10G warm nodes) plus an on-demand auto-scale of 8 x H100 for sustained overflow. This hybrid reduces cost while covering instantaneous spikes.

Operational notes / optimizations:
- KV/prefix caching: expect ~30–45% token compute reduction for multi-turn flows if session-level KV reuse is enabled (depends on hit rate). This materially reduces both committed and burst needs.
- Batching: for short prompts batching helps throughput but watch p99; use small continuous batching windows (5–10ms) and priority lanes for interactive traffic.
- Quantization: 4-bit gives good cost/throughput; test for hallucination/regression as part of pilot.

Pilot recommendation (risk-minimized):
- Start with a 2-node pilot on H100 (or 3x A100) in Private/VPC that mirrors production routing; run a replay of 48h trace and a controlled spike run to validate p99 and autoscale behavior.
- After pilot: propose committing to 6 x H100 + warm pool (6 A10G) + on-demand burst (8 H100) for GA. We can convert the sketch to a costed proposal once Camila confirms preferred SKUs and the 48h trace.

I'll be on the call Thu 07/27 14:00 PT. Camila — please confirm the workshop time and I'll prepare a quick slide with numbers and a short stress-run plan.

— Karthik
